### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c026bb14e8876674728b9afaa46aae1d46d5d5ce` — the merge of head `4f17c0247ddcd19c8253d92a264fec130dd5ff28` into base `9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c026bb14e8876674728b9afaa46aae1d46d5d5ce && git checkout c026bb14e8876674728b9afaa46aae1d46d5d5ce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57 4f17c0247ddcd19c8253d92a264fec130dd5ff28 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57 && git merge --no-ff 4f17c0247ddcd19c8253d92a264fec130dd5ff28

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `492b279ac6a98962815a633af7fb83c921a3aef4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/services/service-i18n/src/file-i18n-adapter.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/utils/spec-translations.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, scripts/check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs

Inputs read: card #27086 (body, triage 6461049965, claim 6465570149, dev report 6466622473), PR #27203 body and file list (9 files), `git diff 72629f38..492b279a`, and the 51 check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or checked out; the cited code was read in the live tree.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set, widened at one leaf.** `appTranslationDataShape().apps[APP].label` goes `z.string()` → `z.string().optional()` (translation.zod.ts:954). Nothing else in the hunk moves: `navigation[ID].label` stays `z.string()` (:961), `description` was already optional, the `strictObject` unknown-key refusal and the `name`/`title` → `label` and `nav`/`menu`/`menus` → `navigation` aliases are untouched. **Right**, and exactly the card's Target.
2. **Reach of the shared shape.** The shape is spread into `TranslationDataSchema` (:2099, so `TranslationBundleSchema` :2217), `PlatformTranslationDataSchema` (:2148), `ServedTranslationDataSchema` (:2195) and `TranslationItemSchema` (:2351). The PR body names all five. Is that wider than needed? No: the served door is the per-locale merge of every bundle, so when every bundle for a locale lacks the label the served payload lacks it too and must accept that; the item door is one package's registered bundle, the same author as the bundle door; the platform door shares the shape by design (the :2189 comment on why the derived doors are built from the shape and not `.extend()`), and forking it to keep one leaf required on the platform's own bundles would buy nothing the extract walker does not already enforce (③ and ④.3). **Right.**
3. **Public type surface.** `TranslationData['apps'][string]['label']` becomes `string | undefined`, a widening at the input and a narrowing for any reader that typed it as `string`. Readers checked in the tree: `i18n-resolver.ts:1583` reads it through `?.[attr]` behind a `typeof === 'string' && length > 0` guard; `source-hash.ts` walks leaves generically; the console reads it through i18next (`useObjectLabel.ts:385`); `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.ts` authors `apps.setup.label` and still type-checks. No non-test `.apps[x].label` read typed as `string` was found outside the spec package. `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Type Check UI` are still running on the head and are the gate verdicts for this; the read supports them.
4. **Generated references.** `content/docs/references/system/translation.mdx` (four tables) and `api/protocol.mdx` drop the required tick on `label` and show `label?: string`; consistent with the shape. Read, not reviewed (`check:generated` runs under `Lint · docs & code guards`, in progress).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27086-module-bundle-contributed-nav.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, each line-initial with the value first after the colon. The PR body carries the same two lines under Verification. **Both carriers agree.**
- **Kind.** The rule text (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3) names "a requirement tightened" as `narrowed`; this diff is that requirement loosened, and it newly accepts a shape a metadata author can write (an app entry with no label), so the symmetric reading is `added`. Triage's "not a new key, so not a protocol addition" was a triage remark, not a ruling; `none` would put the changeset at `patch`, and a bundle that `defineStack`, `os validate` and `tsc` all refused yesterday and accept today is a protocol change, not a non-protocol widening. `added` ⇒ at least `minor` on a moved package; `@objectstack/spec` is the one package whose `src/**` moves, graded `minor`. **Right.**
- **Gate.** `Check Changeset` ran twice on this head: run 40672371636 (started 10:28:18) `failure`, superseded by the `edited` re-run 40672424390 (started 10:28:42) `success` on the same commit; the earlier run's `PR-body guards` was cancelled by the re-run and the re-run's is `success`. The newest run governs. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Spec property liveness` success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Skills-docs: none** (PR body). `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:169` lists the `apps` group's keys as "(label, description, navigation)" without a requiredness claim and its examples author a label; no `skills/**` file spells `apps.APP.label` as required. Answered.
- **Main moved after the branch point** (dev: 11 commits, none touching the diff's files). On today's `origin/main` the files in this diff have no commit since `72629f38`. Answered; CI runs on the merge commit regardless.
- **Dogfood battery and the full cli unit tier not run locally.** `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` on the head (its shards skipped: no dogfood path changed); `Test Core (1/8 … 8/8)` are in progress and are the verdict for the cli tier.
- **`check:i18n-walk-parity` exited 3 locally (needs a build).** Read: `scripts/check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs` compares the translation GROUPS the spec declares with the groups the extractor walks (:5, :435). A leaf going optional inside the `apps` group cannot move it. The lint jobs that carry it are in progress.
- **`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally.** Neither reads a schema leaf's requiredness; CI `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and `Build Core` are in progress.
- No `open_questions` block in the PR body; no dev flag left unanswered.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`, judged against the card's two acceptance items and against every consumer of the leaf.

1. **Runtime merge (card acceptance 2).** `FileI18nAdapter.loadTranslations` (file-i18n-adapter.ts:172) folds each package's bundle through `deepMerge` (:44-66), which copies the target and recurses only where both sides hold an object; a key absent from the source is never written. Owner-then-module keeps the owner's label because the module entry has no `label` key; module-then-owner takes it from the owner. The new `file-i18n-adapter.test.ts` block pins both orders and `t('apps.crm_enterprise.label')`. **Holds.**
2. **What renders when the only bundle for a locale lacks the label.** Console: `useObjectLabel.ts:385` `appLabel` = `resolve('apps.APP.label', appDef.label ?? appDef.name)`, and `resolve` (:157) probes i18next with `defaultValue: ''` and returns the fallback on an empty or key-echo answer; `spec-translations.ts` copies the `apps` group verbatim into the i18next resource, so an absent leaf is an absent key. Server `/meta`: `translateApp` (i18n-resolver.ts:1613) does `lookupAppAttr(...) ?? doc.label`, and `lookupAppAttr` (:1576) accepts only a non-empty string. In both paths the app's declared label renders; never `''`, never the raw key. `FileI18nAdapter.t()` does echo the key on a miss (:152), but no production caller resolves `apps.APP.label` through bare `t()`; the one hit is a test. **Holds.**
3. **Coverage and `os i18n check` / `extract` for the OWNING package.** `i18n-extract.ts:1565` derives the expected `apps.APP.label` entry from the declared app (`if (app.label) pushEntry(...)`), and :1583 adds the contributed navigation leaves under the TARGET app from `navigationContributionsOf`. The expected set never consulted the schema's requiredness, so an owner whose bundle drops its app label is still reported missing, and a module-only stack is owed only its contributed navigation leaves. That is what `extract` already emitted for a module stack; the old schema refused the extractor's own output, which is the inconsistency the card measured. Making the leaf optional hides no gap. **Holds.**
4. **Lint `translation-target-unknown`.** `validate-translation-references.ts:1997` keys on `apps.APP` and `rawApp.navigation` only, already tolerates `apps: { crm_app: {} }` (its own test :1923), and already accepts the contributed ids under an app the stack only contributes into (`contributedOnlyApps`). Unchanged and consistent with the new door. **Holds.**
5. **Spec pin (card acceptance 1).** `translation-contributed-nav-bundle.test.ts` types the module-only literal as `TranslationData` / `TranslationBundle` (compiled by the test type-check, so TS2741 is pinned), parses it through strict `defineStack` and the bare `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, and controls the navigation leaf at both layers (`@ts-expect-error` plus the issue path) and an authored label round-trip. `translation-contributed-nav-validate-door.test.ts` pins the `os validate` exit code for real. The three layers the card named are each pinned once. **Holds.**
6. **Attempt to break it — explicit `undefined` (should-fix, not a FAIL).** Before this diff a bundle literal `apps: { crm_enterprise: { label: undefined, navigation: {...} } }` was refused (`z.string()`); now `.optional()` accepts it and zod 4 keeps the present-but-undefined key, and `deepMerge`'s else branch (`result[key] = sVal`, :62) then writes `undefined` over the owner's label when that bundle loads second. Reachable only from a TS/JS literal (JSON cannot carry `undefined`), and only when a module author writes the key it has no reason to write. **Should-fix:** have `deepMerge` skip a source value of `undefined`, or pin the case, in a follow-up. The TSDoc's "whichever bundle merged last would win" already states the scalar-overwrite rule this rests on.
7. **Attempt to break it — the empty entry.** `apps: { crm: {} }` is now a valid entry with no anchor leaf (`picklists` keeps `options` required; `apps` keeps nothing). Coverage still reports the owner's missing label (③.3), lint treats it as the app's entry, and the runtime merges nothing. Harmless noise; noted, no finding.
8. **The TSDoc.** Names the contribution surface (`manifest.navigationContributions`), the owning package as the label's author, the deep-merge, and the last-wins cost of restating. Accurate to the code read in ④.1. Holds.

Remainder of the diff (tests, docs, changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. One observation outside `hits`, not a finding: `i18n-standard.mdx:1074` hangs the "label may be left out" clause on the `apps.{app}.navigation.{id}` row; the `apps.{app}` row (:1073) is where a reader looks for it.

**Check-runs on the head at review time:** 25 success, 11 skipped, 1 cancelled and 1 failure (both the superseded first `pr-automation` run, re-run green on the same head), 13 in progress: Test Core (1/8 … 8/8), Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record overrides none of them.

Must-fix: none.
Should-fix: ④.6 — `deepMerge` lets a present-but-`undefined` `apps.APP.label` in a later-loaded bundle clobber the owner's label, a shape the old schema refused.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-s51v9e`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-28T11:07Z

Head `4f17c0247ddcd19c8253d92a264fec130dd5ff28`. Card #27086 (triage `6461049965`), claim `6465570149`, dev report `6466622473`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER for `translation.zod.ts`. The review (`6466797171`) at `492b279a` was a PASS with no must-fix. It found:
  - Only one leaf moves: `apps.APP.label` is optional, and `navigation.ID.label` stays required. The five doors that share the shape are justified.
  - No non-test reader types the label as a `string`. The console falls back to the app's declared label, and `/meta` `translateApp` falls back to `doc.label`. Neither renders an empty string or the raw key.
  - `os i18n extract` derives the owning package's expected `apps.APP.label` from the declared app, so a real gap in the owner's bundle is still reported.
  - `added` is the right kind for a requirement that was relaxed.
- **Since then:** `d1cd3c5e` closes the should-fix. Service-i18n's `deepMerge` now skips a source value that is `undefined`, so a bundle with a present-but-`undefined` label can no longer erase the owner's label. Pins cover both load orders, and an ablation turns the owner-first case red. The docs clause moves to the `apps.{app}` row. `@objectstack/service-i18n` joins the changeset at minor. `4f17c024` merges `main` (no rebase) with no conflicts. The seat applied the round-2 body delta.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #27086`, 10 files, +319/−14. One root changeset, with `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-i18n` at minor. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. `check-governed-merges --pr 27203`: NOT governed, 333 changed lines.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head are 42 success, 11 skipped and 0 red. `mergeable_state` is clean.
- **Landing:** Tier S. `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in this act.
